summary: The article profiles four local innovators who showcased inventions during this year's Local Technology and Innovation Week: Liz Harmon's emotion-aware AI platform CerebraNet, Miguel Torres's algae-powered Algaegy, Simone Patel's QuantumMesh quantum network, and Jordan Liu's GreenBlock modular building system. It then explains the technologies behind them (AI, biotech and renewable energy, quantum networking, sustainable smart design) and argues the city is becoming a global tech hub.
one_line: Profiles of four local inventors (CerebraNet, Algaegy, QuantumMesh, GreenBlock) and the technologies behind them, framing the city as a rising tech hub.
key_facts: The article is dated as of September 15, 2023 and refers to this year's Local Technology and Innovation Week.
Elizabeth "Liz" Harmon, known as the "AI Whisperer," created CerebraNet, an AI platform that improves machine-learning algorithms' ability to process emotional intelligence.
CerebraNet was launched on October 9, 2023 and lets AI recognize human emotions and respond in a contextually appropriate manner.
Harmon's work is relevant to industries such as customer service and healthcare.
Miguel Torres, the "Energy Alchemist," unveiled Algaegy on October 21, 2023, a bio-photovoltaic system that uses photosynthesizing algae to generate electricity.
Algaegy is described as environmentally friendly, highly efficient and scalable, and supports decentralized energy production for homes and businesses.
Simone Patel, the "Connectivity Maestro," introduced the QuantumMesh network on September 25, 2023.
QuantumMesh uses quantum entanglement to transmit data over long distances with no time lag and high security, with potential uses in finance, online gaming and remote surgery.

Jordan Liu, the "Eco-Architect," showcased GreenBlock on November 3, 2023, a modular building system made from upcycled materials integrated with smart technology for energy conservation and automation.
GreenBlock aims to reduce construction waste and dramatically cut the carbon footprint of new buildings.
The article names four key technology areas: AI and machine learning, biotechnology and renewable energy, quantum computing and networking, and sustainable design with smart technologies.
The article concludes that the local innovation ecosystem is thriving and that these inventions could address global challenges.
